I've read the model and verified it with the Structurizr tooling (parse/validate/inspect — all read-only; the file on disk is untouched, and the DSL itself is syntactically valid). Here's my review, walked as a C4 document.

## Elements

- **`tariff` (Tariff Rules Library)** — Modeled as a `container`, but it's a library. A rules library consumed "in-process" by the Rate Service is not a C4 container; containers are deployable units or distinct building blocks (apps, databases, queues). A library is a component-level artifact. *Why it matters:* it inflates the container view with a non-deployable unit and misrepresents the architecture. It should be a component inside the Rate Service (or omitted at this level).

- **`payments` (Payment Gateway) and `loyaltyFeed` (Loyalty Points Feed)** — Both are modeled as generic `element`s, but both are external software systems. In C4, external systems are `softwareSystem`s (tagged external), not generic elements. *Why it matters:* generic elements lose the C4 semantics — they aren't recognized as systems, can't carry system-level properties, and are inconsistent with how the model types its other systems.

- **`legacy` (Legacy Booking System)** — Orphan: it has no relationships to/from it and appears on no view (the tooling flags it as disconnected and absent from all views). *Why it matters:* a disconnected element communicates nothing. If the legacy system is being phased out, there should be a relationship (e.g., data migration into Stay Planner), or it should be removed from the model.

- **`payments` vs `loyaltyFeed` — inconsistent external marking** — `loyaltyFeed` is tagged `External`, but `payments` is not, even though both are external systems. *Why it matters:* the model doesn't uniformly distinguish internal from external elements, which affects view rendering (externals are usually styled differently) and reader clarity.

## Relationships

- **`portal -> rate` — description "uses"** — Too vague. C4 relationships need a meaningful verb phrase describing the interaction. *Why it matters:* "uses" doesn't tell the reader what the portal does with the rate service; it should read like "Requests stay rates from."

- **`rate -> tariff` — technology "in-process"** — "in-process" is a deployment/interaction style, not a technology or protocol. *Why it matters:* C4 relationship technologies should be concrete (HTTP, gRPC, SQL, Kafka). This is also a symptom of the tariff-as-container problem — a library isn't something you call over a protocol.

## Views

- **Container view — auto-generated key** — The view has no explicit key, so it gets an auto-generated one (`Container-001`) that isn't guaranteed to be stable over time. *Why it matters:* references to the view (docs, links, tooling) can break if the key changes. It should have an explicit, stable key.

- **System Context view (`GuestContext`) — loses the mobile entry point** — The guest has two relationships to the system (via portal and via mobile), but when collapsed to the system level only one is shown ("Books rooms through"). *Why it matters:* the Level 1 view doesn't reflect that guests can also book via the mobile app, so it under-represents the guest's journey — which is the view's stated purpose.

## Workspace / completeness

- **Workspace — no scope defined** — The workspace has no scope (should be `Landscape` or `SoftwareSystem`). *Why it matters:* without a scope, the model's boundaries are less well-defined and tooling can't reason about what the workspace represents.

- **`planner` (Stay Planner) — missing documentation** — The system has containers but no documentation attached. *Why it matters:* the system's purpose, context, and rationale aren't captured in the model, reducing its value as an architecture document.

- **`planner` (Stay Planner) — missing decisions** — The system has containers but no architectural decisions recorded. *Why it matters:* the rationale behind key choices (why Kafka, why this service split) isn't captured, so the model doesn't explain *why* the architecture is the way it is.

- **`mediadb` (Media Database) — description broader than its relationships** — The description says it stores "contracts, invoices, and guest media," but the only relationship to it is `feedback` storing "guest feedback media." *Why it matters:* contracts and invoices are mentioned but connected to no element, so the description overstates what the model actually shows (minor consistency issue).

---

**Summary:** the DSL is syntactically valid and the two views are at the right C4 levels, but the model has real C4-convention problems — a library typed as a container, two external systems typed as generic elements, an orphaned legacy system, inconsistent external tagging, two weak relationship descriptions/technologies, and several workspace-completeness gaps (no scope, no documentation, no decisions, an unstable view key). The most consequential are the element-typing issues (`tariff`, `payments`, `loyaltyFeed`) and the orphaned `legacy` system, since those misrepresent what the architecture actually is.
